text: One windy autumn evening in Paris. <break time="0.8s" /> I was sitting in silence. <break time="0.8s" /> With my friend C, Auguste Dupin. <break time="0.8s" /> In his small library. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was dark. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly the door opened. <break time="0.8s" /> And in walked Monsieur G. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect of the Paris police. <break time="0.8s" /> An old acquaintance of ours. <break time="0.8s" /> Dupin rose to light a lamp. <break time="0.8s" /> But he sat down again. <break time="0.8s" /> When the Prefect said. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted advice. <break time="0.8s" /> About an official matter. <break time="0.8s" /> If it is a problem. <break time="0.8s" /> That requires thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Dupin. <break time="0.8s" /> We shall examine it better in the dark. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That the case was very simple. <break time="0.8s" /> But very odd. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dupin replied. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps the mystery is a little too plain. <break time="0.8s" /> At this. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect roared with laughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Crying that nobody had ever heard. <break time="0.8s" /> Of such a foolish idea. <break time="0.8s" /> Then having made us promise. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep it secret. <break time="0.8s" /> He told us. <break time="0.8s" /> That a letter of great importance. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been stolen. <break time="0.8s" /> From the royal apartments. <break time="0.8s" /> The thief, he said. <break time="0.8s" /> Was the Minister D. <break time="0.8s" /> A bold, clever man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was now using the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> To gain power over its owner.
